name: Advanced Filesystem: Backup
description: File backup manager with batch/cron/queue support and multiple storage backends (Local, FTP/FTPS, Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Google Cloud Storage). ZIP or file-by-file mode, retention, restore and download.
project_description: The Backup sub-module of Advanced Filesystem archives the site's stream-wrapper file trees (public://, private:// and any other local wrapper) to one or more storage backends. It provides a pluggable BackupStorage plugin type with five built-in backends — Local filesystem, FTP/FTPS, Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2 and Google Cloud Storage — the three cloud backends sharing a native AWS Signature v4 implementation over Drupal's Guzzle client (no SDK). Backups run in two modes: ZIP (a single chunked archive built with ZipArchive) or file-by-file (each file streamed straight to the backend, no temp disk). Runs can be triggered interactively via the Batch API, in the background via a phased queue worker, or on cron; a state lock prevents concurrent runs and a run-history table records status, file counts, size and errors. Retention prunes old archives per backend. Admins can download an archive or restore it (chunked ZIP extraction / file re-download back to the original URIs) from a dashboard. Glob exclusion patterns, selectable schemes and per-chunk sizing are configurable. Every route is gated behind the restricted 'administer advanced_filesystem_backup' permission.
